---
title: "About"
subtitle: "Who we are, and why we answer strange questions about the brain."
---

Notes from the Neuropil is currently written by the Connectomics team at the Allen Institute, but we welcome contributions!

We are scientists who work on generating large volumetric maps of what neural tissue 
looks like and how cells are connected in those circuits. The [MICrONS dataset](https://www.microns-explorer.org/)
was a recent example, in which our team mapped a cubic millimeter of mouse visual cortex at synaptic resolution.

As more people explored the data, we noticed that they were often finding structures that many people on our team were unfamiliar with themselves!
Often these findings reveal things we don't (yet) understand ourselves or have never seen before - and that is the exciting part of doing science!
We wanted to have a place to collect these observations from students, scientists, and curious 
members of the public, and share what we think people are looking at in Neuroglancer.

So -- please share your observations with us! Click the submission form above to get in touch.
